# Epistle of Barnabas — Chapter 16 (EMET Literal)

**Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, Epistle of Barnabas 16
**Agent:** EMET (Literal)
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

1. Furthermore I will also speak to you concerning the temple, how those wretched people were led astray and set their hope on the building, as if it were the house of God, rather than on their God who made them.
2. For almost like the pagans they consecrated him in the temple. And what does the Lord say? "Learn: 'Who has measured the heaven with his span, or the earth with his palm? Have I not?' says the Lord. 'Heaven is my throne and the earth is my footstool: what kind of house will you build for me, or what place shall be my resting place?' says the Lord." You know that their hope is vain.
3. Furthermore again he says: "Behold, those who demolished this temple will themselves build it."
4. It is happening. For on account of the war it was demolished by the enemies; now the servants of the enemies will build it up again.
5. Also, it was made known that the city and the temple and the people of Israel were to be given up. For the scripture says: "And it shall come to pass in the last days, that the Lord will give up the sheep of the pasture and the sheepfold and their watchtower to destruction." And it happened as the Lord spoke.
6. Let us then inquire whether there is a temple of God. Yes, there is — where he himself speaks and makes an entrance. For it is written: "And it shall come to pass when the week is completed, a temple of God shall be built gloriously in the name of the Lord."
7. I find therefore that there is a temple. How then shall it be built in the name of the Lord? Learn: before we believed in God, the abode of our heart was corrupt and weak — truly a house built by human hands, because it was full of idolatry and was the house of demons, since we did everything contrary to God.
8. But it shall be built in the name of the Lord. Take heed that the temple of the Lord may be built gloriously. How? Learn: having received the forgiveness of sins, and having set our hope on the Name, we became new, created again from the beginning; and so God truly dwells in our abode, that is, in us.
9. How? The word of his faith, the calling of his promise, the wisdom of his righteous ordinances, the commandments of his teaching, himself prophesying in us, himself dwelling in us — opening to us who had been enslaved unto death the door of the temple, which is the mouth, and giving us repentance, leading us into the incorruptible temple.
10. For the one who desires to be saved looks not to the human being but to him who dwells in him and speaks in him, being amazed that he never either heard these words from the mouth of the speaker, nor himself desired to hear them. This is a spiritual temple being built to the Lord.
